families.bigger-codes: Error-correcting codes where every codeword has equal weight: pushing the limits on how many words fit.
families.biggest-graphs: How big can a network get if every node has few links and any node is a few hops from any other?
families.codetables-binary-linear: Codes that catch and fix errors in data. More space between codewords means more errors can be fixed.
families.codetables-qubit-upper-bounds-n101-256: Quantum codes protect fragile qubits from errors. These results lower the ceiling on how good they can be.
families.eaqecc-qutrit-codetables-gaps: Quantum codes boosted by shared entanglement, built on qutrits instead of qubits. Better codes fix more.
families.erdos-699-binomial-gcd: An Erdős puzzle about Pascal's triangle: do entries in the same row always share a big enough prime?
families.faster-matrix-multiplication: Recipes that multiply grids of numbers, the math inside AI and graphics, using fewer steps.
families.group-testing-separable-designs: Pooled testing designs: mix samples so cleverly that you can still pinpoint which ones are positive.
families.hadamard-maxdet-records: A classic puzzle: fill a square grid with plus and minus signs to make its determinant as big as possible.
families.lehmer-past-10-to-the-50: Can a non-prime number have a quirky property that every prime has? Lehmer asked long ago. Still open.
families.lennard-jones-ccd-doye-table: Find the lowest-energy way for atoms to clump into a cluster: a classic test of how matter takes shape.
families.ncbi-pathogen-ast-ecoli-genotype-phenoty: Reading a germ's genes to predict whether an antibiotic still works on it. Superbugs are a growing threat.
families.packomania-hyperspheres-hsp4-hsp6: Fit equal balls inside a bigger ball in higher dimensions and make them as large as possible.
families.packomania-scu-spheres-in-cube: Pack a set number of equal spheres into a cube, as big as they can be. Like stacking oranges, but hard.
families.qoblib-market-split-and-portfolio: Hard money-allocation puzzles from a benchmark library built to test quantum and classical solvers.
families.risk-or-safety-exact-optimal-play: Exact winning odds in a coin-tossing game where players bank points or risk them, with perfect play.
families.robust-forecast-aggregation-bounds: How well can you blend forecasts from several experts without knowing how they work? Mapping the limits.
families.robustbench-cifar100-stronger-attack: Fool an image-recognition AI with tiny pixel tweaks, showing it is less robust than its public score says.
families.stable-marriage-max-stable-matchings: Nobel-winning matchmaking math: how many stable ways can a group be matched so nobody wants to elope?
families.sunflower-free-capacity-lower-bound: Pick as many small sets as you can without any of them forming a 'sunflower'. Tied to famous open problems.
families.thomson-problem-live-tables: Arrange charged particles on a sphere so they repel each other as little as possible. Classic physics.
families.vnncomp-2026-unsolved-instances: Find inputs that trick a neural network into breaking a safety rule, in cases verifier tools left open.

categories.unbroken-ciphers: Secret messages and cipher challenges nobody has cracked yet, from wartime machines to puzzle setters.
categories.undeciphered-scripts: Ancient writing nobody can read, like Linear A and the Indus script. Wins are testable predictions.
categories.ancient-texts: Piecing together broken clay tablets and papyri, and restoring lost signs, scored against hidden answers.
categories.herculaneum-scrolls: Scrolls burned by Vesuvius: find the ink in scans so the papyri can be read without unrolling them.
categories.number-hunts: Hunting special numbers and hard limits by computer, from huge exact searches to Busy Beaver machines.
categories.erdos-and-proofs: Open questions from mathematician Paul Erdős: find counterexamples, settle small cases, check proofs.
categories.record-tables: Codes, designs and packings that beat the best entries in public tables kept by experts.
categories.graphs-games-automata: Networks, puzzles, tilings and simple rule-based worlds like the Game of Life.
categories.packings-physics: Packing circles and spheres, and finding the lowest-energy shapes of atom clusters, against live tables.
categories.algorithms: Faster recipes for core computing tasks, like multiplying matrices in fewer steps.
categories.optimization-benchmarks: Better delivery routes, schedules and plans on public benchmark sets that solvers compete on.
categories.sky-archives: Spotting new variable stars and possible planet transits hiding in public telescope data. Candidates only.
categories.ml-robustness: Showing AI models are easier to fool than their scores say, or that safety checkers miss cases.
categories.disease-research: Cancer, rare diseases, superbugs and outbreaks: computer predictions on public data, never medical advice.
categories.drug-discovery: Predicting how molecules behave and stick to their targets, scored on public drug-discovery leaderboards.
categories.biology: Protein, DNA and evolution puzzles with public scorecards, from designing RNA to reading individual cells.
categories.physics: Exact counts, tight limits and precise constants in physics, from magnets and lattices to quantum info.
categories.earth-and-sky: Missed quakes, meteors and solar flares hiding in open science archives, checked against official catalogs.
